content: Side Effects: It is possible for your child to experience fever, pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. These are common side effects. Please remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to your child outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of all possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding any side effects. Precautions: Before administering palivizumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if your child has any known allergies to this medication or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication is not typically used in adults and is unlikely to be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. If you have any questions about this medication, consult your doctor. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products your child uses, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Be aware that this medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as RSV diagnostic tests or virus culture tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. Overdose: In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: It is crucial to ensure that your child receives each scheduled dose of this medication as directed. Missing doses may reduce the effectiveness of the treatment. Storage: Storage instructions are not applicable for this medication, as it is typically administered by a healthcare professional. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your child. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your child’s specific health needs. How to Use: Before your child begins treatment with palivizumab, and before each injection, read the patient information leaflet provided by your healthcare professional. This medication is administered by a healthcare professional as an intramuscular injection, typically into the thigh, once a month during RSV season. In the Northern Hemisphere, RSV season generally begins in October and ends in April. To maximize the benefits of this medication, ensure that your child receives it regularly as prescribed. Additional Notes: Adding plans to your healthcare management allows you to compare the formulary status of this medication with other drugs in the same class. For the most accurate and up-to-date formulary information, contact the relevant plan provider.
